content.comment_body: I have 5 running [product_name] devices that have been in use for several years with the same model and hardware type. About 4 years ago, I purchased a 6th [product_name], but it stayed unused until now. I have been operating the existing devices on software [version_no], and they worked well. When I tried to upload or download a program to the sixth device, I was unable to do so with [version_no]. After upgrading to a newer version of the software, uploading and downloading worked without any issues. This was thanks to advice found in previous support tickets. However, I still encounter an issue with online testing—the error message states: 'Online test failed. The hardware type of [product_name] in [product_name] software does not match the connected [product_name] device.' Could someone please explain, in simple terms and ideally with screenshots, how to ensure matching hardware types? In the online settings, I can see the firmware version for the new device is 1.83.01, while the older devices show 1.81.03 and hardware type [product_name][version_no]. After re-uploading/downloading, the version for the device updated and I was then able to successfully run the online test.

During online testing, the program and device type in the [product_name] software must match the actual [product_name] hardware exactly. If the wrong device type is chosen in the software, you will see error messages, and online connections cannot be established—even if some parameter values do not match, such as time settings, constants in functions, or counter starting values. A helpful tip: first switch the device to stop mode, download the program from the device into the software, then start the online connection in the software, and only then restart the program on the hardware.

analysis.insight_summary: The user is facing compatibility and synchronization challenges between [product_name] hardware and its project configuration in [product_name] software. The core issue lies in mismatches between the firmware or hardware type set in the software and that present on the device, which prevents successful online testing. Once both software and hardware firmware and types are properly matched, the issue is resolved, demonstrating that correct device selection and configuration alignment are critical for smooth operation.
analysis.user_expectations: The user expects that adding identical hardware should be straightforward, with upload/download and online testing working automatically, without the need for manual adjustments of firmware or hardware type settings. They seek step-by-step instructions, preferably with images, to resolve matching and synchronization problems.
